notebooks.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems
notebooks.summary: Autonomous systems increasingly utilize multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to pursue self-generated goals. Recent developments, specifically Pareto-Conditioned Proximal Policy Optimization (PC-PPO) and FairDICE, provide mechanisms to learn non-dominated policy portfolios and handle constrained optimization, allowing navigation of reliability-efficiency frontiers without retraining. However, the field still faces fundamental challenges regarding non-convex optimization and strict convexity assumptions in scalarization functions.
notebooks.findings:
FairDICE extends the DICE RL framework to optimize sample-based algorithms, balancing trade-offs between objectives and welfare under convexity assumptions. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]

DICE-based approaches relying on Lagrangian duality assume convexity and do not cover all forms of non-convex scalarization. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]
notebooks.limitations: Current autonomous objective discovery mechanisms are heavily influenced by underlying optimization assumptions; while PC-PPO and FairDICE address certain scalarization and fairness limits, effective handling of broad non-convex scalarization and long-term, self-directed objective prioritization remains an open challenge.
notebooks.next_questions: How can DICE-based frameworks be extended to non-convex scalarization functions to support broader autonomous objective discovery?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook findings to integrate FairDICE convex scalarization limits and multi-objective optimization constraints.

notebooks.title: Integrating Autonomous Multi-Agent Frameworks and Curiosity-Driven Exploration for Open-Ended Discovery
notebooks.summary: Autonomous problem formulation benefits from multi-agent collaboration and intrinsic curiosity. However, systemic limitations—such as non-convex scalarization in objective learning—constrain the ability of these systems to independently prioritize diverse, non-trivial research problems.
notebooks.findings: Intrinsic curiosity bootstraps exploration, but successful autonomous inquiry requires overcoming non-convex scalarization hurdles when defining what problems to investigate. [source-feb4fddb33664d63] [source-4668e4bd26fe43c7]
notebooks.limitations: Autonomous systems currently lack robust mechanisms to bridge the gap between curiosity-driven exploration and the systematic formulation of complex, non-convex research objectives.
notebooks.next_questions: Can multi-agent frameworks explicitly model and reformulate their own objective functions to overcome non-convexity constraints? How do agents verify if a self-generated research problem is both novel and solvable?

detail.title: Integrating Autonomous Multi-Agent Frameworks and Curiosity-Driven Exploration for Open-Ended Discovery
detail.summary: Autonomous problem formulation benefits from multi-agent collaboration and intrinsic curiosity. However, systemic limitations—such as non-convex scalarization in objective learning—constrain the ability of these systems to independently prioritize diverse, non-trivial research problems.
detail.findings: Intrinsic curiosity bootstraps exploration, but successful autonomous inquiry requires overcoming non-convex scalarization hurdles when defining what problems to investigate. [source-feb4fddb33664d63] [source-4668e4bd26fe43c7]
detail.limitations: Autonomous systems currently lack robust mechanisms to bridge the gap between curiosity-driven exploration and the systematic formulation of complex, non-convex research objectives.
detail.next_questions: Can multi-agent frameworks explicitly model and reformulate their own objective functions to overcome non-convexity constraints? How do agents verify if a self-generated research problem is both novel and solvable?
detail.reason: Revising to integrate the constraint of non-convex scalarization identified in the objective discovery research.

nodes.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems

detail.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems
detail.summary: Autonomous systems increasingly utilize multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to pursue self-generated goals. Recent developments, specifically Pareto-Conditioned Proximal Policy Optimization (PC-PPO) and FairDICE, provide mechanisms to learn non-dominated policy portfolios and handle constrained optimization, allowing navigation of reliability-efficiency frontiers without retraining. However, the field still faces fundamental challenges regarding non-convex optimization and strict convexity assumptions in scalarization functions.
detail.findings:
FairDICE extends the DICE RL framework to optimize sample-based algorithms, balancing trade-offs between objectives and welfare under convexity assumptions. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]

DICE-based approaches relying on Lagrangian duality assume convexity and do not cover all forms of non-convex scalarization. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]
detail.limitations: Current autonomous objective discovery mechanisms are heavily influenced by underlying optimization assumptions; while PC-PPO and FairDICE address certain scalarization and fairness limits, effective handling of broad non-convex scalarization and long-term, self-directed objective prioritization remains an open challenge.
detail.next_questions: How can DICE-based frameworks be extended to non-convex scalarization functions to support broader autonomous objective discovery?
detail.reason: Revising notebook findings to integrate FairDICE convex scalarization limits and multi-objective optimization constraints.
